CHIEF COMPLAINT
Cough for one week.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Billy is a 74-year-old patient who presents with a cough that started approximately one week ago. He reports that over the last two days his symptoms have worsened. He has been coughing up yellow sputum and reports not feeling well. He denies fever but notes feeling warm without having checked his temperature. He denies chills but reports feeling achy at times. He denies shortness of breath. He reports nasal congestion with postnasal drainage and some sinus pressure. No one else in his household is sick. The patient works as a teacher. Additionally, the patient reports that this morning while coughing, he fell down approximately four to five stairs and injured his right knee. He has been able to walk since the fall but reports pain mostly on the inside of his knee with a slight limp. He denies the knee feeling like it will give out. He has taken over-the-counter Dayquil for cough and cold symptoms with minimal relief but has not taken anything for knee pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies fever, chills, or shortness of breath. He reports nasal congestion, postnasal drainage, and sinus pressure bilaterally. He reports feeling achy. He denies other systemic symptoms.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
1. Hypertension
2. Diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
1. Lisinopril 20 mg daily
2. Metformin 1000 mg twice daily
3. Over-the-counter Dayquil (patient-initiated)

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient works as a teacher. He is married. He does not monitor his diet or sodium intake, stating he relies on his blood pressure medication. He does not check his blood pressure or blood glucose levels at home.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital Signs: Temperature 98.4°F, Blood Pressure 125/62 mmHg, Heart Rate 80s, Oxygen Saturation 97% on room air.
Facial Exam: Pain to palpation of bilateral maxillary sinuses.
Nasal Exam: Erythema and edema of nasal turbinates bilaterally with yellow discharge.
Throat Exam: Uvula midline. No erythema, edema, or exudate in peritonsillar space.
Neck Exam: Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy.
Lung Exam: Coarse rhonchi present bilaterally that clear with cough.
Heart Exam: Regular rate and rhythm. No murmur appreciated.
Right Knee Exam: Pain to palpation. Decreased flexion and extension. Ecchymosis to right medial knee. No effusion.

RESULTS
Vital signs as documented above. Physical examination findings as documented above.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Cough/Viral Syndrome with Mild Bronchitis: Continue over-the-counter supportive care. Prescribe guaifenesin 600 mg twice daily to help with expectoration. No antibiotics at this time. Patient instructed to call if symptoms worsen; will consider chest X-ray to rule out pneumonia.

2. Right Knee Pain/Right Medial Collateral Ligament Strain: Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily. Refer to physical therapy for strengthening exercises. Order right knee X-ray to rule out bony injury.

3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order lipid panel. Encourage patient to monitor blood pressure and diet, including sodium intake.

4. Diabetes Mellitus: Continue metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Order hemoglobin A1c. Encourage patient to monitor sugar intake and report blood glucose values through patient portal.
